# Frequently Asked Questions

What is Veterinary Cancer Concierge Services?

Veterinary Cancer Concierge Services is a specialized service dedicated to providing comprehensive cancer care for pets. Our team of board-certified veterinary oncologists offers expert consultations, personalized treatment plans, and a range of support services to ensure the best possible care for your pet.

What types of cancer do you treat in pets?

We treat a wide variety of cancers in pets, including but not limited to lymphoma, osteosarcoma, mast cell tumors, hemangiosarcoma, and melanoma. Our team is experienced in diagnosing and treating both common and rare forms of cancer in dogs and cats.

How do your Telemedicine services work?

Our telemedicine services allow you to connect with one of our veterinary oncologists via secure, high-definition video calls or via a phone call (depending on the day and what is more convenient for you). You can schedule an appointment, discuss your pet’s condition, review diagnostic test results, and receive a personalized treatment plan from the comfort of your home or preferred environment.

What do I need for a Telemedicine appointment?

For a telemedicine appointment, you will need a stable internet connection and a device with a camera and microphone (such as a smartphone, tablet, or computer). In some cases the telemedicine appointment will be done via a phone call, and a computer/tablet or internet connection would not be necessary in this case.

Can more than one person be present at the time of a Telemedicine Consultation?

Yes, as many people as you would like can attend the consultation, whether this is done by video conferencing or by phone. We will make sure to email the video conference link prior to the appointment (if done by video conferencing) or conference them in directly (if done by phone). Multiple people can join the consultation, even if they are not in the same location.

Can I get a second opinion through a telemedicine consultation?

Yes, our telemedicine services are an excellent way to get a second opinion on your pet’s cancer diagnosis and treatment plan. Our oncologists will review all of your pet’s medical history, examine prior veterinary visit records, and provide expert recommendations.

What can be done during an at-home or mobile visit and what types of treatments do you offer?

With an at-home or mobile visit, we bring our veterinary cancer care directly to you and your pet. Our team will come to your home (or meet at a convenient location if outside of our travel range), and will perform any necessary testing and treatment in our mobile suite. We offer a range of treatments including chemotherapy, targeted therapy, immunotherapy, and palliative care. Our oncologists will develop a personalized treatment plan based on your pet’s specific type of cancer and overall health.

How do I schedule an At-Home or Mobile Visit?

Once your pet’s telemedicine consultation has been completed, you can schedule an At-Home or Mobile Visit by contacting us directly via phone or email.

What areas do you serve with At-Home and Mobile Visits?

Our service area covers a variety of locations in Connecticut and New York. This includes Fairfield County in Connecticut, encompassing Stamford, Darien, New Canaan, Greenwich, Norwalk, Rowayton, Westport, Fairfield, Weston, and Wilton. In Westchester County, New York, we serve Scarsdale, Armonk, Mamaroneck, Larchmont, and Yonkers. Additionally, we reach Mount Kisco, Bedford Hills, Harrison, and Pound Ridge. While we cannot directly service New York City, we would be happy to discuss meeting at a location mutually agreed upon outside of the city for a mobile visit.

Does my pet need a confirmed diagnosis prior to scheduling a consultation or appointment with VCCS?

No. Our doctors at VCCS will consult with any client when they are concerned their pet may have cancer, even if a diagnosis has not yet been confirmed. For these patients our doctors will discuss all diagnostic options and help guide you through the appropriate next steps to try and get a more definitive answer.

## Veterinary Cancer Concierge Services

At Veterinary Cancer Concierge Services (VCCS), we understand the challenges and stresses of managing your pet’s cancer diagnosis and that navigating this process can be overwhelming. That is why we are dedicated to crafting tailored treatment plans that address diverse cancer-related issues with precision and care. Our team is committed to supporting both pets and their families through every stage of the cancer journey. From managing complex diseases to discussing therapy options and facilitating treatment, we provide comprehensive care that prioritizes your pet’s well-being. With VCCS, you can expect unwavering dedication, compassionate support, and innovative solutions designed to enhance the quality of life for your loved one.

As a mobile oncology concierge practice serving Fairfield and Westchester Counties, we bring testing, treatment, and palliative care directly to you and your beloved pet. Our boutique-style practice offers a unique solution, allowing cancer patients to receive blood work, urine testing, x-rays, additional testing, chemotherapy, and other cancer treatments in our state-of-the-art mobile suite without ever leaving home. This adds convenience and reduces anxiety and stress associated with traveling to a veterinary clinic or large hospital. We also offer medical and radiation oncology telemedicine consultations for clients seeking guidance for their pet’s cancer care.

## We Simplify Logistics

For patients requiring frequent evaluations and/or treatments, our mobile service simplifies logistics, improving scheduling and enhancing the overall quality of life for pets and their families. We pride ourselves on our collaborative approach, working closely with your family veterinarian or any other clinician/veterinary hospital involved in your pet’s care. This ensures a comprehensive and coordinated treatment plan.  At VCCS, we are dedicated to providing exceptional care tailored to your pet’s individual needs, ensuring comfort, convenience, and peace of mind every step of the way. Our service area covers a variety of locations in Connecticut and New York. This includes Fairfield County in Connecticut, encompassing Stamford, Darien, New Canaan, Greenwich, Norwalk, Rowayton, Westport, Fairfield, Weston, and Wilton. In Westchester County, New York, we serve Scarsdale, Armonk, Mamaroneck, Larchmont, and Yonkers. Additionally, we reach Mount Kisco, Bedford Hills, Harrison, and Pound Ridge. While we cannot directly service New York City, we’re happy to meet at a convenient nearby location to examine and/or treat your pet.

Please note: For clients outside our travel range who wish to see us, we are happy to arrange to meet at a convenient location. This is usually in Stamford, New Canaan, or Greenwich. However, we are open to other options depending on our schedule and the location of our travel each day. ×

Dr. Lindsay Thalheim’s passion for veterinary oncology, combined with her exceptional credentials and commitment to excellence, make her an authority in the field. ## Tara McNama

## LVT

Tara McNama is a seasoned Licensed Veterinary Technician (LVT) with a profound dedication to animal care and welfare. With over two decades of experience in the veterinary field, Tara’s journey began in 2000, following her graduation from Fordham University with a degree in Finance/Economics. Determined to pursue her passion for animal medicine, Tara enrolled at Mercy College, where she obtained her degree in Veterinary Technology in 2003.

Throughout her career, Tara has acquired diverse experiences and specialties. She has been a licensed LVT since 2005, with extensive experience in general practice from 2000 to 2010, emergency medicine from 2010 to 2011, and oncology from 2011 to the present. Her dedication to providing high-quality care and her commitment to ongoing learning have made her a respected and valued member of the veterinary community.

In the summer of 2023, Tara joined Veterinary Cancer Concierge Services and assumed the role of Head Veterinary Technician. In this capacity, she oversees the administration of anticancer therapies on-site and leads and trains other technicians and assistants, ensuring that patients receive the highest quality of care. Tara’s compassionate approach and dedication to her patient’s well-being make her an invaluable asset to the team as she strives for excellence and ensures that patients and their families are comfortable during their cancer care journey. Her unwavering commitment to providing the highest standard of care reflects her deep-rooted dedication to making a difference in the lives of her patients.

Born and raised in New Rochelle, NY, Tara now resides in Fairfield, CT, with her husband and their two sons. Their household is filled with love and companionship, shared with four cherished pets: Logan, a 3-year-old Alaskan Malamute; Charlotte May, an 11-year-old Chihuahua Mix; George Monkey, a 5-year-old DLH; and Birdie, a 6-year-old DLH.

Tara’s passion for working with animals has been a lifelong pursuit, stemming from her childhood dreams. She finds immense fulfillment in sharing her wealth of knowledge and insights with her colleagues, leveraging her experiences and continuing education to educate clients and enhance patient care.

Dr. Anne Marie Nock brings compassionate, competent and ethical veterinary medicine to your door. Find answers to our most common questions below.

What is your service area?

We routinely travel to towns in Hartford County, including: East Windsor, Windsor, South Windsor, Windsor Locks, Granby, East Granby, Simsbury, Suffield, Enfield, Somers, Ellington, Vernon, Bolton, Manchester, Glastonbury, East Hartford, West Hartford, Wethersfield, Newington, Farmington, Avon, and Bloomfield.

We have had to make some restrictions on locations we are able to service as some neighborhoods make it difficult to navigate such a large vehicle. If this is the case we would be happy to service you at our clinic location.

How does your service work?

We are a mobile veterinary clinic that visits you and your animal at your home. The major difference between our fees and those of a regular veterinary clinic is our fee to come to your location. This is called a "House Call" fee and varies based on your location.

Our new clinic in East Windsor, CT is ready to see appointments. Clinic appointments do not have an associated "House Call" fee.

Can you see an animal in my house?

Yes. We often see elderly animals that have difficulty with mobility or animals that are afraid to leave the house.

We ask that your animal is in either a confined room, on a leash or inside a carrier so your appointment time is not wasted on staff chasing your animal.

How can I schedule an appointment?

Call us at (860) 682-0354. We can travel to your house or you can come to us at one of our locations in East Windsor or South Glastonbury, CT.

NOTE: We are no longer accepting new clients due to maximum client capacity.

What is the length of the appointment?

We spend 35 to 45 minutes with your pet. Please have cats in carriers and ready to be seen so that this time is not spent finding your pet.

What are the charges for you to examine my pet?

There is a house call fee, which begins at $80 and depends upon how far we have to travel.

There is also an exam fee, depending on the type of exam: • Yearly wellness exam: $70 • Sick animal exam fee: $75 • Emergency fee: $145

What forms of payment do you take?

We accept cash, check and credit cards. We do not keep credit cards on file.

What are your protocols due to the COVID-19 pandemic?

We are taking the upmost precautions due to the pandemic to make sure you and your pet stay healthy! We are still safely performing house calls maintaining proper social distancing and our team continuing to wear masks.

Our current procedure is parking our 28-foot mobile unit in your driveway for an exam. If you are able to, animals can be brought out on a leash or inside a carrier for examination. If not we please ask that you wear a mask as our team enters your home to perform necessary services.

Starting her role in January 2026, Zap brings significant experience to the position, having previously served as a relief vet at DAWS since 2023. She also runs her own mobile veterinary practice, Integrative Veterinary Care, serving Connecticut, New York, and New Jersey. Her appointment follows the passing of longtime DAWS vet Dr. Cary Brenner, and was strongly supported by DAWS Executive Director Adam Carley, who praised her proactive medical approach and vision for the shelter.

Zap is deeply committed to collaborative and compassionate care, working closely with pet owners and fellow staff. A Ridgefield native, she holds degrees in veterinary science, toxicology, and veterinary medicine from the University of Connecticut, the University of Florida, and St. George's University, respectively. In addition to her clinic work, she actively participates in global and regional animal welfare initiatives with organizations such as World Vets and Caribbean Spay Neuter. She is preparing to join a spay and neuter mission in Belize this April. At DAWS, Zap looks forward to mentoring staff and launching new community programs, including pet loss support and Safe Tails for animals rescued from crisis situations.
Meanwhile, Zap kept Taffy's human foster caregiver up-to-date on the feline's health and anticipated health care needs.
"I want to be a vet for somebody the way I would want someone to be a vet for me," said Zap, 43. "I think it's really important to listen to my clients and hear what my clients are saying ... It's not going to be a good team for the animal if the owner feels they aren't being listened to."
In addition to her work with DAWS, Zap runs her own ambulatory veterinary practice, Integrative Veterinary Care, providing mobile veterinary services, house calls and farm calls in Connecticut, New York and New Jersey.
Zap lives in Ridgefield along with her dog Enzo, her ball python Monty, tortoises Henry and Harry, several hives of honeybees and a horse named Topaz.
While Zap officially became the shelter's primary veterinarian this year, she said she has worked as relief veterinarian there since 2023. Before his death, former primary vet Cary Brenner called Zap to see if she'd fill in at the shelter when needed.

Veterinary dermatology practice wins approval for new Darien location at Old Kings Highway North (https://www.ctinsider.com/news/article/darian-unleashed-veterinary-dermatology-stratford-22218878.php)

Falk chose Darien for its proximity to an existing client base and increasing demand for accessible pet dermatology services. The expansion aligns with a growing global market in veterinary dermatology, driven by rising pet ownership and skin conditions in animals.
Veterinary dermatology practice wins approval for new Darien location at Old Kings Highway North
Date: Sun Apr 26 09:00:15 2026 UTC

DARIEN - A family-owned veterinary dermatology practice in Stratford is opening a location in Darien.
Unleashed Veterinary Dermatology plans to open at 50 Old Kings Highway North in a 9,000-square-foot, two-story office previously occupied by Hartford HealthCare. The practice will occupy the entire second floor of the building, while Hartford HealthCare will remain on the first floor.
The Planning & Zoning Commission on Tuesday approved a zoning change allowing specialty veterinary office uses in the business zone - uses that more closely resemble medical offices than traditional veterinary clinics. The change takes effect May 10.  It does not include veterinary hospitals, walk-in clinics, kennels, or any veterinary use requiring overnight boarding of animals.
At a March 10 public hearing, attorney Amy Zabatakis, of Rucci Law Group, said the veterinary dermatology practice functions much like a human dermatology office.
